ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
17. Four charges $Q_1$, $Q_2$, $Q_3$ and $Q_4$ of same magnitude are fixed along the $x$ axis at $x = -2a$, $-a$, $+a$ and $+2a$, respectively. A positive charge $q$ is placed on the positive $y$ axis at a distance $b > 0$. Four options of the signs of these charges are given in List I. The direction of the forces on the charge $q$ is given in List II. Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists.

List I
P. $Q_1$, $Q_2$, $Q_3$, $Q_4$ all positive
Q. $Q_1$, $Q_2$ positive; $Q_3$, $Q_4$ negative
R. $Q_1$, $Q_4$ positive; $Q_2$, $Q_3$ negative
S. $Q_1$, $Q_3$ positive; $Q_2$, $Q_4$ negative

List II
1. $+x$
2. $-x$
3. $+y$
4. $-y$

method.method_draft: Use symmetry and qualitative force comparison. Read from the diagram that Q1 and Q4 lie symmetrically at x=-2a and x=+2a, Q2 and Q3 lie symmetrically at x=-a and x=+a, and q is on the y-axis above the origin. From the text, take Q1 and Q4 as positive, Q2 and Q3 as negative, all with equal magnitude, and q as positive. Pair Q1 with Q4: their horizontal force components on q cancel, and because they repel positive q, their vertical resultant is upward. Pair Q2 with Q3: their horizontal components cancel, and because they attract positive q, their vertical resultant is downward. Since Q2 and Q3 are closer to q than Q1 and Q4, the downward inner-pair force is stronger than the upward outer-pair force. Therefore the net force is along -y.

method.method_draft: Compute the signed y-component of the electric field at q. Read from the diagram/text the coordinates Q1=(-2a,0), Q2=(-a,0), Q3=(+a,0), Q4=(+2a,0), and q=(0,b). Assign charges +Q to Q1,Q4 and -Q to Q2,Q3. For a charge at x=s on the x-axis, the field at (0,b) has y-component kQ_i b/(s^2+b^2)^{3/2}. Summing the symmetric outer and inner pairs gives E_y = 2kQ b/(4a^2+b^2)^{3/2} - 2kQ b/(a^2+b^2)^{3/2}. Since (a^2+b^2)^{3/2} < (4a^2+b^2)^{3/2}, the negative inner-pair term has larger magnitude, so E_y<0. The x-components cancel by symmetry, and because q is positive, the force direction is the same as the field: -y.
